description:
Ultra-Smooth Chocolate Soft Serve Ice Cream made at home

This chocolate soft serve ice cream recipe is formulated specifically for soft-serve draw temperatures, not hard-pack ice cream. The balance of fat, sugar, milk solids, cocoa, and guar gum is engineered to deliver a smooth, elastic texture at –6 °C, with clean melt and zero chalkiness.

In this video, I break down why soft serve recipes are different, how cocoa affects texture, and how a small amount of guar gum dramatically improves mouthfeel and stability.

The only real non commercial soft serve ice cream machine worth looking at for a semi large production is this one: https://tinyurl.com/3h5y2nhb
It's the push button version though, the touch screen version has screen issues. The Gormia machine here actually does a really good job with the right recipes as you can see in this video. No hidden anything from me, no "edits" to make stuff look perfect etc, just REAL recipes making REAL ice cream. 

⸻

⏱️ Timestamps

00:00 – Intro
00:17 – Why is REAL soft serve different?
01:38 – Full ingredient list and assembly
04:23 – Rested, now let's churn it
05:01 – The "Pull"
05:08 – Why's,, What's and How's + Outro

⸻

🍫 Chocolate Soft Serve Ice Cream Recipe (915 g total)

Ingredients
 • Whole milk (3.25%): 480 g
 • Heavy cream (33-36%): 200 g
 • Skim milk powder: 40 g
 • Sugar (sucrose): 140 g
 • Unsweetened cocoa powder (10% fat): 50 g
 • Salt: ~1 g
 • Vanilla extract: ~4 g
 • Guar gum: 0.25 g

⸻

📌 Why This Works
 • Correct freezing-point depression for soft serve
 • High cocoa load without dryness
 • Minimal guar for elasticity, not gumminess
 • Smooth melt and clean finish
